FACT-1.gloss: Gretchen has a total of 110 coins

FACT-2.gloss: There are 30 more gold coins than silver coins

RULE-1.gloss: If a person has a total number of coins and the number of gold coins equals the number of silver coins plus a difference, then there exist silver and gold coin counts that satisfy the two equations
RULE-1.formula: ∀p∀T∀d((TotalCoins(p, T) ∧ GoldIsSilverPlus(p, d)) → ∃S∃G(SilverCoins(p, S) ∧ GoldCoins(p, G) ∧ G = S + d ∧ G + S = T))

RULE-2.gloss: If there exist SilverCoins(p, S) and GoldCoins(p, G) with G = S + d ∧ G + S = T, then S = 40 ∧ G = 70 for the specific numbers T = 110 and d = 30
RULE-2.formula: ∀p∀S∀G((SilverCoins(p, S) ∧ GoldCoins(p, G) ∧ G = S + n_30 ∧ G + S = n_110) → (S = n_40 ∧ G = n_70))
RULE-2.verify_reason: embeds a concrete arithmetic result (S=40, G=70) into the rule instead of a general algebraic relation

INF-1.gloss: From FACT-1, FACT-2, and RULE-1 by Modus Ponens with Universal Instantiation
INF-1.formula: ∃S∃G(SilverCoins(gretchen, S) ∧ GoldCoins(gretchen, G) ∧ G = S + n_30 ∧ G + S = n_110)

INF-2.gloss: From INF-1 and RULE-2 by Existential Instantiation and Modus Ponens
